title: Swot Analysis of Django vs Flask
text:
A sleep and study habits project needs a simple website to recruit student participants. They need a site with a short description of the study, an eligibility screener of about eight questions, and a sign-up form that collects a name and email for people who qualify. Ideally, research assistants could also log in and see a list of sign-ups. Since site will hold contact information, security and privacy matter, campus IT will want to know how the data is stored. The graduate student has never built a website, and the lab may re-use the website for future studies. The website will not be maintained full time. What would be a better choice to solve this problem: Django or Flask?
Simple Conclusion: Django would be a better fit because using Flask without much experience is more likely to have security risks than Django.

title: Swot Analysis of Django vs Flask
text:
Django

Strengths

Built in security features protect your website from:

Cross-site scripting (XSS) protection
SQL injection protection
Clickjacking protection
Read here for more

Sanitizes user input by default (Cleans it to remove harmful elements)
Has built in databse management

Weaknesses

Steep learning curve for a beginner, since it is a full-stack web framework vs. a micro one
A bit heavier than what the project requires (it only needs a simple website)

Opportunities

Since Django is a full web-framework, the lab could build upon this website. for other surveys
More boiler-plate, but requires less code than Flask if it scales project if they need patient data for another survey.

Threats

Website may require updates, or security features could go out of date

title: Swot Analysis of Django vs Flask
text:
Flask

Strengths

Easy learning curve, since it is a micro-web framework
Ideal for smaller scale projects like these
A lot of freedom (relies on developer’s skills)

Weaknesses

No built in security features, requires extra effort from the developer to protect against things that Django protects against automatically
No built in user management, forcing the inexperienced web developer to rely on external libraries.
A lot of freedom (relies on developer’s skill)
Does not have built in database management (Requires external libraries)
Does not sanitize user input unless done manually.

Opportunities

As long as scope stays small, Flask will be easier for another team to understand if the project is handed off

Threats

Bad actors could steal data if the developer doesn’t manually put safety precautions.
Code re-use could be harder if the application grows.
